summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and esophageal varices, was admitted due to black stools with streaks of bright red blood over two days, concerning for gastrointestinal bleeding. He was hemodynamically stable with a hemoglobin drop from 9.2 to 7.9. He was managed with octreotide infusion, IV antibiotics, and oral PPI. An EGD showed no active bleeding, only small erosions, and a small bowel endoscopy was unremarkable. His hemoglobin stabilized at 8.4, and he did not require transfusion. Blood pressure medications were held initially and restarted at reduced doses. He remained stable, abdominal pain improved, and he was discharged home with instructions to pursue outpatient colonoscopy, continue liver support medications, avoid alcohol, and follow up with primary and specialty care.
